evidence_summary: Ive's ≤26 milestones are cofounding Tangerine and joining Apple design at 25. Father-domain apprenticeship and intense early design reps are the core advantage; world-famous product impact (iMac onward) came after Jobs's return, still built on that early placement.

name: Harley Finkelstein
milestone_by_age_26: Founded a university T-shirt / apparel business at age 17 while at McGill (~2000–2001), scaling nationally—a dated entrepreneurial founding well before joining Shopify in 2010 (~age 26–27) and later b
early_history_summary: Born November 8, 1983 in Montreal; raised partly in South Florida. Founded first company at 17 at McGill, later earned law degree and MBA at University of Ottawa, then joined Shopify early (store #137 / full-time ~2010) rising to COO and President.
evidence_summary: Finkelstein's clear ≤26 milestone is founding a scaled apparel business at 17. Shopify presidency is later (joined ~2010 at ~26–27); eligibility rests on the teen company, not cofounding Shopify (Lütke/Weinand/Lake).

name: Anthony Pompliano
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Digaforce (social media analytics) around 2013 at about age 25 and sold it the same year; also founded/exited early startups after Army service before Facebook PM role (~2014–15, age ~26).
early_history_summary: Born June 15, 1988; U.S. Army sergeant with Iraq service. After military, founded early tech startups including Digaforce (acquired 2013), then product/growth roles at Facebook and Snapchat before becoming a prominent Bitcoin investor, podcaster, and fund manager.
evidence_summary: Pompliano's ≤26 material milestone is founding and selling Digaforce ~2013 at ~25 after military service. Later crypto fame (Morgan Creek Digital, Pomp Podcast) is post-26. Scores conservative given uneven primary-source depth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Army/Iraq, early startups, Facebook growth, crypto media

name: Brewster Kahle
milestone_by_age_26: Helped start Thinking Machines Corporation around 1983 at about age 22–23 after MIT, serving as lead engineer on parallel supercomputing—material early founding/engineering leadership well before WAIS
early_history_summary: Born October 21, 1960 in New York City; B.S. MIT 1982 studying AI with Marvin Minsky and Danny Hillis. Joined/helped found Thinking Machines as lead engineer, later invented WAIS (1989), sold WAIS Inc. to AOL, cofounded Alexa Internet and founded Internet Archive (1996).
evidence_summary: Kahle's ≤26 milestone is early leadership at Thinking Machines right after MIT. Later WAIS/Alexa/Internet Archive define his public legacy but the early parallel-computing founding engineering role qualifies under age rule.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT AI Lab, Minsky/Hillis, Thinking Machines, early internet search

name: Brendan Iribe
milestone_by_age_26: Cofounded Scaleform in 2003 at about age 23–24 with Michael Antonov, building the leading game UI middleware company later sold to Autodesk (2011); Oculus CEO role came later (2012+).
early_history_summary: Born August 12, 1979 in Maryland; attended University of Maryland. Cofounded Scaleform (game UI tech), sold to Autodesk, worked at Gaikai, then became founding CEO of Oculus VR recruited by Palmer Luckey after Kickstarter success.
evidence_summary: Iribe's ≤26 milestone is cofounding Scaleform at ~24, a real middleware company with eventual Autodesk exit. Oculus CEO/Facebook acquisition wealth came later (~33–35).
primary_early_advantage_tags: Scaleform, Antonov partnership, game middleware, later Oculus CEO

name: Michael Antonov
milestone_by_age_26: Cofounded Scaleform around 2003 during/after college (~age 23) as CTO, building widely embedded game UI middleware later sold to Autodesk; later Oculus chief software architect.
early_history_summary: Immigrated from post-Soviet Russia to the U.S. as a teen (~age 14 around 1993 per interviews); studied computer science at University of Maryland; cofounded Scaleform with Brendan Iribe; later Oculus software lead; subsequent biotech/AI ventures (Deep Origin).
evidence_summary: Antonov's Scaleform cofounding/CTO role ~2003 at ~23 is the ≤26 milestone. Immigrant self-directed CS path plus durable Iribe partnership; Oculus software leadership and later Deep Origin are subsequent chapters.
primary_early_advantage_tags: immigrant engineer, UMD, Scaleform CTO, Iribe partnership, Oculus

name: Nate Mitchell
milestone_by_age_26: Cofounded Oculus VR in 2012 at about age 24–25 (Dickinson College class of 2009) and helped lead product as the company Kickstarted the Rift and scaled toward Facebook acquisition (2014, age ~27).
early_history_summary: Dickinson College '09; joined Palmer Luckey early to cofound Oculus, serving in product leadership (VP Product / Head of Rift). Later founded Mountaintop Studios and joined Sesame as CPO.
evidence_summary: Mitchell cofounded Oculus at ~25, a clear ≤26 material founding event on the VR wave with Luckey/Iribe team. Exact birth date less public than classmates' graduation year implies ~1987; Facebook exit and Mountaintop/Sesame are later.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Oculus cofounder, Luckey partnership, VR wave, product leadership

primary_early_advantage_tags: podcast distribution, cold outreach, London tech scene, Atomico exposure

name: Akshay Kothari
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Pulse, a mobile news aggregation app, at Stanford in May 2010 (launched App Store 12 May 2010) at about age 24; app was demoed by Steve Jobs and later sold to LinkedIn for ~$90M.
early_history_summary: Indian-born engineer who earned an EE BS at Purdue and MS at Stanford (2008–2010). With classmate Ankit Gupta in a d.school Launchpad course, built Pulse in about six weeks for the iPad launch wave, then scaled it before joining Notion as co-founder/COO.
evidence_summary: Kothari used Stanford's Launchpad course and the 2010 iPad wave to ship Pulse, which Jobs publicly praised and LinkedIn later acquired. Advantage is elite-school product pipeline plus complementary cofounder, not inherited capital. Later helped scale Notion after joining as co-founder/COO.

name: Simon Last
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Notion with Ivan Zhao around 2013 at about age 23, serving as technical co-founder/CTO on the all-in-one workspace product that later became a multi-billion-dollar company.
early_history_summary: Engineering-focused co-founder who partnered with Ivan Zhao in the early 2010s; sources describe him as in his early twenties when hired/partnered for Notion. The duo rebuilt Notion after a near-failure period and shipped the product that defined modern modular workspaces.
evidence_summary: Last is consistently described as Notion's technical co-founder from ~2013 (CSV birth 1990 → ~age 23). The pair nearly shut down, then rebuilt the product; advantage is complementary cofounder intensity and product craft rather than documented family capital. Public biographical detail is thinner th
primary_early_advantage_tags: Zhao partnership, full-stack rebuild, product craft, SF startup scene

name: Josh Kopelman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Infonautics in 1992 as a Wharton sophomore at about age 20; company IPO'd on Nasdaq in 1996 when he was still in his mid-twenties.
early_history_summary: Raised in Great Neck, NY; father a Baruch professor, mother a real-estate broker. At Wharton (grad 1993) co-founded Infonautics, took it public in 1996, then founded Half.com (sold to eBay 2000 for ~$300M) and later First Round Capital.
evidence_summary: Kopelman founded Infonautics as a Wharton undergrad (~1992), IPO'd it by ~age 24–26, then built Half.com and First Round. Family was professional/academic rather than tech-heir; primary edge was elite school + early internet timing + repeated founding reps.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Wharton, Infonautics IPO, early internet, Philadelphia tech

name: Jessica Mah
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded inDinero in 2009 at age 19 with Berkeley classmate Andy Su, building financial/accounting software for startups; entered Y Combinator and scaled the company through her early twenties.
early_history_summary: Born 18 May 1990 in Westchester County, NY to Hong Kong immigrant entrepreneurs in clothing. Finished high school at 15, Simon's Rock, then UC Berkeley CS by ~19. Ran internet businesses from age 11–13 (server resale, eBay computer parts) before inDinero.
evidence_summary: Mah's path is unusually early: middle-school businesses, college at 15–17, inDinero at 19, YC, Forbes/Inc recognition. Family provided entrepreneurial norms and likely financial stability without a software dynasty. Clear ≤26 founding milestone with multiple sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen entrepreneurship, Berkeley CS, YC, Su cofounder, immigrant business family

name: Andy Su
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded inDinero in 2009 with Jessica Mah as Berkeley CS classmates at about age 19–20, serving as technical co-founder/CTO of the accounting/finance platform.
early_history_summary: UC Berkeley computer science student who roomed/partnered with Jessica Mah to prototype inDinero during college. Served as technical leader through early fundraising and product pivots; later founded Pry Financials and other companies.
evidence_summary: Su is documented as inDinero co-founder/CTO at ~19–20 (Inc. profile said age 20 in 2011). Technical half of a complementary founding pair; family background less documented than Mah's. Clear ≤26 founding milestone.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Berkeley CS, Mah partnership, YC, early fintech SaaS

name: Dennis Crowley
milestone_by_age_26: Created Dodgeball, a pioneering location-based mobile social service, around 2000–2003 (NYU ITP era) at about age 24–26; sold to Google in 2005 when he was ~28–29.
early_history_summary: Born 19 June 1976 in Medway, Massachusetts. Built personal web projects after college; after a Vindigo layoff at ~25, developed Dodgeball as an SMS check-in network that became a landmark pre-smartphone location product, later reborn as Foursquare (2009).
evidence_summary: Crowley's Dodgeball work in the early 2000s (age mid-20s) is a clear pre-26/at-26 material product milestone later acquired by Google; Foursquare (2009) was the post-26 reboot. Advantage is domain immersion in urban social location rather than inherited capital.
primary_early_advantage_tags: location social, SMS check-ins, NYC nightlife domain, NYU ITP, Dodgeball
